name: St. Petersburg (United States)

colors.symbolism: the waters of Tampa Bay and the Gulf of Mexico
the waters of Tampa Bay and the Gulf of Mexico

description: Five equal horizontal bands of orange, red, green, blue and navy parted by narrow white fimbriations, charged with a large white pelican in silhouette perched on a rock, spanning the full height of the flag and facing the hoist.

features.role: brown pelican in white silhouette, perched on a rock
features.symbolism: environmental concern; the pelican is indigenous to the area and became the city's mascot

history: Adopted 17 February 1983 to a design by the city's graphic designer Ronald F. Whitney Jr., after officials judged the previous seal-based flag hard to reproduce or recognise. St. Petersburg's first flag dates from 1927, designed by Mayor C. J. Maurer with a committee of city officials. The pelican, indigenous to the area, was chosen to stand for environmental concern; it became a city mascot and lent its name to the Feed the Pelican Fund, which supports the birds through the winter.
